artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan closing three contract/validator drift threads: lint-enforced plan-level Status ownership boundary across 13 implementation agents, a shared M1/M2/M3 Status-grammar library wired into validate-artifact.sh at error level, the report-heading conformance remedy, and fan-out plus bidirectional marker/commit-synchrony sections in phase-closure.md.

memory_candidates.content: This agent-system repo has exactly two established mechanisms for preventing 'contract/skeleton text drifts from what a validator enforces' defects, and a plan for any such defect should be built on one of them rather than inventing a third. (1) AGENT-BODY TEXT: a canonical fragment under agent-system/extensions/core/context/contracts/ (e.g. no-task-references-bullet.md, return-meta-artifacts-template.md) holding the exact text in a fenced block plus a stated classification rule, with a check in scripts/lint/lint-agent-contracts.sh that reads the expected text FROM the fragment at runtime (never hardcoded) and greps a curated in-scope agent list. The lint runs as gate 6 of verify-deploy.sh. Note that @-references inside an agent body do NOT auto-resolve at subagent spawn time, which is why literal copies plus a lint are used instead of an include. (2) SCRIPT LOGIC: a shared library under scripts/lib/ (e.g. phase-heading-patterns.sh) sourced lazily via a ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}-relative path that resolves identically in the source store and the deployed .claude/ tree, with a missing library treated as a loud environment error (a distinct exit code), never a silent fallback to an inline pattern. Corollary: context/contracts/*.md files ARE load-bearing for extension agents when @-referenced from their Context References section - phase-closure.md is referenced 'always load'/'MANDATORY' from every implementation agent, making it the right home for a single normative statement rather than copying a paragraph into 13 files.
